method: the probes run against the superseded builds themselves, not a reconstruction and not a defect switch

witnesses.claim: the pinned R1 file is the build the verifier reviewed
R1 accepted a case with NO task id, transition, artifact digest or target role
R1's idempotency key had 3 of R1P-04's 5 components
R1P-04 tests (1)(2)(3) were UNRUNNABLE against R1
witnesses.superseded_behaviour: no task/transition/artifact/role is accepted, so duplicate suppression and target rejection have nothing to key on

witnesses.claim: R1's ActionRequest payload did not carry the key to the target
R1's /sink produced the represented side effect with no capability, no case and no authorization
R1 wrote a live token verbatim under an unrecognised key
R1 destroyed authority_id / authority_version / tokens_used
...and the replacement was a bare constant the harness scores PRESENT, hiding the loss
R1 let a REJECT be overwritten by an ACCEPT and then minted an ActionRequest for the rejected case
R1's pending branch wrote NO capture
R1's owner-key refusal wrote NO capture
R1 hardcoded the candidate, so two providers shared one corpus
witnesses.superseded_behaviour: candidate field in records: {'<absent>'}; path segment: 'stub'

witnesses.claim: R1 wrote no stub-minted timestamp on any capture
R1 accepted a provider-authored decision field on these routes
R1 let the provider choose run_id and silently overwrote the run — resetting started_at and emptying checkpoints
R1's reconcile asserted certainty and cited ACT-01 for a run that does not exist
witnesses.superseded_behaviour: -> 200 {"reconciled": true, "side_effect_certain": true, "note": "post-state checked before any r

witnesses.claim: R1's triage asserted provider conduct it cannot observe
R1 landed a live token in a capture as a rejected key name
a non-ASCII owner key raised TypeError before any authorization verdict
a TRUTHY non-dict metadata crashed the handler, while the FALSY [] the review's illustrative repro used returned 200 — which is why 13_ VC-01 requires the truthy case
the pinned R2 file is the build returned at R2
R2 had no /owner/artifact/register: there was no owner-registered digest for a provider-supplied one to be checked against
...so R2 opened a case on a provider-supplied artifact_digest alone, with no registration_ref and nothing to bind it to
R2 ran every RESPONSE through the same redaction as a capture, so over a real socket the resume token it had just minted came back as a descriptor and no provider could ever carry it
...and the in-process path returned the token intact, which is why the R2 suite passed 56/56 while the service was unrunnable: that suite called dispatch(), below the response path
witnesses.superseded_behaviour: dispatch() token is a str, HTTP token is a dict

witnesses.claim: R2 took authority from a provider-supplied `origin` field: content the provider authored came back recorded as owner-authorized
...and R2 had no idea_ref, no stored owner content and no owner_content_digest to compare a copy against
witnesses.superseded_behaviour: 'idea_ref' appears 0 times in the R2 source

witnesses.claim: R2 had neither /owner/reconcile nor /poc1/reconcile, so an uncertain delivery had no route to any resolution at all
...and RECONCILED_NOT_DELIVERED did not exist in R2, so the owner-attestation rules Rev 5 makes testable had nothing to bind to
witnesses.superseded_behaviour: 'RECONCILED_NOT_DELIVERED' appears 0 times in the R2 source

witnesses.claim: R2 wrote one record per event with no prepared/committed pair, so a write interrupted after the state moved left authority effective with no record that it had moved
R2 drew every capture from a single budget, so a provider flooding refusals competed for the same space an owner decision needed
R2 had no ROUTE_POLICY table: caller, credential, field list, envelope rule and quota pool were spread through handler bodies, so 'delete a policy row and the suite fails closed' had no row to delete

R2 minted a SECOND run for the same schedule occurrence instead of the 409 that preserves the prior started_at and checkpoint count — the duplicate declaration POC-3 exists to measure was recorded as an ordinary new run
witnesses.superseded_behaviour: second run-started -> 200, run_id run-71d1be3efe37 vs run-2aa8b090342d, run records now 2
